leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Apply TypeScript interfaces to define a structured user authentication state object
Implement React hooks (useState) to create and manage local authentication state within a component
Use the localStorage API to store authentication tokens and user data persistently in the browser
Define event handler functions to respond to user login and logout actions
Construct a custom React hook (useAuth) to encapsulate authentication logic and state management
Utilize the useEffect hook to initialize authentication state from localStorage on component mount
Execute the storage event listener to detect changes to localStorage made in other browser tabs
Handle storage events to synchronize authentication state across multiple tabs when changes occur
Apply conditional rendering to display different UI components based on the current authentication status
Implement cleanup functions within useEffect to remove event listeners when components unmount
Control component re-renders by properly updating state in response to storage events
Return authentication state and handler functions from the custom hook for consumption by React components
